narration: Rhythms of Fire: The Living Tradition of Azerbaijani Folk Dance
This is Azerbaijani folk dance. Ancient to modern.

Title card: Azerbaijani folk dance · Azerbaijan · Ancient to modern

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The history of Azerbaijani dance extends back to prehistoric times, supported by Mesolithic rock carvings at Qobustan and Nakhchivan that depict figures engaged in circle dances.
Ritual dances evolved through the Middle Ages into distinct forms practiced during festivities and palace gatherings.
The first professional state dance ensemble was established in 1938, followed by the formation of groups like Chinar in 1959.
on_screen: Map: Azerbaijan · Middle East
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dances mark life events, particularly weddings (such as bride processions and celebrations) and Nowruz spring festivals celebrating fertility and renewal.
They express community unity, hospitality, athletic prowess, and humour.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dances are performed in solos, pairs, or large circles.
Women's technique centers on the upper body, arms, hands, and facial expressions, constrained by the flowing movement of traditional skirts.
Men's technique relies on athletic footwork, including rising onto the toes and dropping to the knees.
Watch for Yally circle hold, Toe and knee drop.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (VlSeUtRN6g4)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Concentric circles, lines, triangles, and solo/couple staging

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music relies on 6/8 and 3/4 meters, featuring instruments such as the balaban, nagara drum, and dayereh (qaval).
Melodies frequently draw from mugham modes like Seygah, Mahur, and Shushter, blending quick tempos with lyrical phrasing.
Listen for the balaban, nagara, dayereh.
The pulse is 6/8 and 3/4.
Characterized by quick tempos and traditional eastern melodies driven by the reedy tone of the balaban and the punchy accents of nagara drums.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Traditional costumes are exceptionally well preserved, featuring colourful, ornate garments for women and pastoral or heroic attire for men.
Performances take place at weddings, Nowruz spring festivals, rural gatherings, and theatrical stages.
on_screen: Image gallery: 6 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include choreographers and dancers Alibaba Abdullayev, Amina Dilbazi, Rosa Jalilova, Afaq Melikova, and composer Uzeyir Hajibeyov, who systematically processed traditional dance melodies.
Regional dances include Abayi and Agir Karadaghi (from Shaki and Zaqatala), Asta Karabagi (from Karabakh), Qazakhi (from Qazakh District), and various forms of Yally such as Kochari and Sharur.
Rooted in ancient Caucasian folk traditions and ritual celebrations, developing through court ensembles into contemporary stage and community practices.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Azerbaijani folk dance is variant of Lezginka: Avari and other Azerbaijani dances accelerate into the quick rhythm of Lezginka music.
Azerbaijani folk dance is sibling of Turkish dance: Shares regional Caucasian and Turkic folk dance motifs.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Azerbaijani folk dance (Azerbaijan). Meter 6/8 and 3/4. Instruments: balaban, nagara, dayereh. Mood: lively, lyrical, energetic. It should sound like this: Characterized by quick tempos and traditional eastern melodies driven by the reedy tone of the balaban and the punchy accents of nagara drums.
